To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have combined physiological, morphological and molecular techniques in order to characterize olfactory neurons in the antennal lorb, the first olfactory brain region in insects.

we have developed a method that allows us to combine physiological and morphological analysis of the same antennal lobe neuron in the honeybee, Apis mellifera, that we have characterized the physiological and morphological properties of a variety of antennal lobe interneurons, that these interneurons can be categorized into two main classes, and that we have identified a relationship between the response properties of these neurons and the innervation of their respective glomeruli.
the response properties of antennal lobe local and projection neurons can be predicted from the innervated olfactory glomerulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the physiology and morphology of individual olfactory neurons.
the relationship between the physiological response properties and the morphology of antennal lobe cells, and with the relationship between glomeruli and their innervation by local neurons.
the relationship between morphology and physiology of antennal lobe olfactory neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the morphology of antennal lobe local neurons determines their physiological response profile.
the morphology of antennal lobe interneurons is not random, but is correlated to their physiological and anatomical properties.
the morphology and physiological properties of local antennal lobe interneurons are closely interrelated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physiological response profile of an olfactory neuron depends not only on its input glomerulus but also on its morphology.
the antennal lombic circuitry has a high degree of functional organization.
the antennal lobre is not a homogeneous structure but is organized in subglomeruli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physiological response properties are not only dependent on the type of sensory neuron, but also on its morphology, i.e. the glomeruli it innervates.
the physiological response properties are highly dependent on the innervated olfactory glomerulus.
a more detailed physiological characterization of antennal lobe local neurons is feasible by combining electrophysiological, calcium imaging and morphological approaches.
